You read one email for a job seeker and say what it means for the application named at the top. Go down these rules and use the FIRST that fits:
1. A job alert, newsletter, survey, event, advert or "X is hiring" mail -> "none".
2. They will not move forward, chose other candidates, it is not a match, or the role is filled or closed -> "rejected".
3. It offers the job -> "offer".
4. It asks you to complete an assessment, test, coding challenge or take-home (a few questions to answer by reply are not one) -> "assessment".
5. It asks to schedule or book a call, screen or interview, or is a calendar invitation for one -> "interview".
6. It only confirms the application was received or will be reviewed, or sends a code to verify you -> "ack".
7. A person from the company asks you a question or for something about this application -> "responded".
8. Anything else, including a different role or a sales pitch -> "none".
The evidence must be a sentence copied from the email that shows the status.
Reply with JSON only: {"evidence": "<copied sentence, max 200 chars>", "status": "..."}

Application: Senior Site Reliability Engineer at Northwind Labs, applied 2026-10-01.

From: no-reply@careers.example.com
Date: Oct 6
Subject: Thank you for applying to Northwind Labs

Alex,
Thank you for your interest in working at Northwind Labs. Your application has been received and will be reviewed by our recruitment team.
Should you be chosen to proceed with the selection process, we will reach out to you through the contact details provided within your application.
